logic_errors.title: A refreshed access grant does not update the permission checkbox and can be unintentionally reversed
logic_errors.finding: AccessManager refetches account/grant rows when refreshed event props arrive, but AccessRow is keyed only by event ID and account ID. Its enabled state is initialized once with useState(initialEnabled), so a newly fetched initialEnabled value is ignored. The displayed checkbox and the next set_event_staff_access payload can disagree with the grant data just fetched from the server.
reproduction: Render the actual AccessManager component with event e1 and a fetched active grant for staff1; select e1 and observe the checked checkbox.

Supply a revoked grant on the next account/grant read and rerender with a fresh object for the same event, matching the event-prop replacement produced by an RSC refresh. The effect runs and the grants are fetched again.
The existing AccessRow remains mounted because its key is still e1:staff1; the checkbox remains checked despite the newly fetched revoked_at value.

Click Save access without toggling the stale checkbox. The component submits set_event_staff_access with p_event_id=e1, p_user_id=staff1 and p_enabled=true, reversing the fetched revocation. The inverse case can revoke a newly granted user. A refresh following another account's save can expose the same problem.
logic_errors.execution_evidence: Independently reproduced with the repository's actual TSX transpiled in memory, React, JSDOM and Testing Library inside the required offline sandbox. Initial active-grant checkbox=true; after a same-event prop refresh with the revoked-grant fixture checkbox=true; clicking Save emitted {name:set_event_staff_access,args:{p_event_id:e1,p_user_id:staff1,p_enabled:true}}. This was a component-state reproduction using a mocked Supabase transport, not an authenticated HTTP/DB integration test. No product or test file was created or edited.
logic_errors.impact: Troy can be shown a permission state inconsistent with a completed refetch and can accidentally re-enable access revoked in another tab/session, or disable newly enabled access. This is a correctness defect in permission management, not a demonstrated RPC/RLS authorization bypass.
logic_errors.required_fix: Reconcile AccessRow draft state with changes to the fetched grant state, or remount the row when the fetched enabled/revoked state changes. Account for pending/unsaved edits explicitly rather than silently retaining stale values. Add regression tests for both enabled-to-revoked and revoked-to-enabled refetches, including a refresh caused by saving another account.
logic_errors.acceptance: After fetching a changed grant for the same event/account, the row reflects that authoritative state or presents an explicit edit conflict; a subsequent save cannot silently submit the old state. Existing grant/revoke tests must remain green.

suggestions.suggestion: The current course-change editor deliberately refuses changes while any nonarchived contest exists and always sends p_contest_placements:null. This is the contract's safe-refusal option, not a partial-remap/data-corruption bug. It is nevertheless a limitation of the original course-edit request: the offered workaround archives existing contests and recreates playable contests rather than remapping the existing ones. Consider a complete placement-remap UI using the backend's atomic placements array, preserving contest IDs, tokens and entries. Keep this limitation explicit rather than describing unrestricted event course editing.

The passing tests correctly exercise useful component and error-handling seams, but most fluent query mocks return the same fixtures regardless of actual filters and none proves PostgREST relationship discovery, RLS, Auth or Storage. Add same-account refresh/conflict coverage for the blocking finding; strengthen query-shape assertions and cross-event/kind library fixtures where practical. Keep actual-service acceptance distinct from these mocks.

Remove or explicitly retire unused legacy mutation actions/components in a follow-up. They still ignore returned errors and some request direct event/contest mutations, but they are not an authorization bypass under the reviewed backend contract: direct client event/contest DML is revoked, review uses the fresh-ACL RPC, legacy sponsor-strip writes are platform/nonarchive restricted, and legacy Storage update/delete policies are removed. The new rendered workflows use checkedMutation. Do not revive these old paths without adapting them to the new contract.

Expand the densely compressed JSX and mutation handlers into normally formatted source. This is an auditability/maintenance judgment, not a documented-standard violation or an additional release blocker.

release_gates.gate: Combine the frontend with the final reviewed backend migration and any parent-accepted backend fixes, then verify against an authorized real local Supabase Auth/PostgREST/Storage stack. The frontend checkout alone does not contain the new migration. Confirm real named RPC dispatch, JSON error results, nested SELECT shapes, persisted mutations and readbacks. The concurrent metadata-only edit/archived-course fix is not adjudicated here; its final revision needs parent verification.

Exercise granted staff, same-organization ungranted owner/admin, revoked creator, no-grant login and platform identities through authenticated requests. Check direct event/settings/entries/print/leaderboard/history/access/catalog URLs and mutation endpoints, including revocation without logout. Signed-out redirects and a public shell are not authenticated integration evidence.

Verify actual local Storage upload and metadata registration, wrong-event/wrong-kind selections, revoked and malformed-path uploads, denied overwrite/update/delete and retained objects after registration/selection failure. Verify public delivery separately. Public event-media URLs remain downloadable by URL holders after revoke/archive; the implementation must not promise revocable image delivery.

Use a real browser for mobile layout, popup loading/error/keyboard/focus behavior, five seconds after image load and once per visit across polling/token navigation, current logo on multiple contest pages, draft print readiness and print pagination. Decode/scan the generated QR against the unchanged legacy-compatible /c/<token> route and exercise remembered golfer, retry UUID, closest-to-pin inches and unmeasured drive claims with a real local backend. JSDOM assertions do not prove browser layout, image timing, pagination or QR scannability.

Before any separately authorized publication, verify the deployed policy/privilege inventory and the trusted Troy/platform-admin identity inventory, approve migration/application ordering and obtain publication approval. No hosted access, real credentials, pushes, deployments, account changes or task completion were performed for this review.

summary: FAIL: one independently reproduced frontend logic defect; no substantiated authorization bypass or exposed secret found. Reviewed frontend HEAD ddb038faf16c15f4be6e881796ccaac5d4d709fe and its implementation diff from 1be624d3f515ada41ab86d4e570bee81301a26a9, the requested planning/requirements/contract/result documents as context rather than proof, all changed production source and component tests, route wrappers, public-player compatibility paths, user-scoped clients and legacy actions. Compared every new rendered RPC name/parameter set and checkedMutation result expectation to the actual backend migration at immutable commit 9800799dde5ebfc64da9bd3cf89239664c0d1b63; no mismatch found. Source review found server platform guards beyond hidden menus, fresh RLS event reads without service-role fallback, operational/archive separation, event-filtered and kind-filtered media selection, immutable upload/register/select sequencing without destructive orphan cleanup, snapshot-based placement, current parent-event logo and authenticated draft print, and the 5000ms post-load captured-per-visit banner with dismissal/error and token reset handling. Independently reran the existing UI suite in the required sandbox: 65 tests passed in 12 files (exit 0), with the existing nonblocking Vite config-loader warning. A separate in-memory component reproduction exposed the stale permission-row defect that those tests miss. Scoped git diff --check passed and frontend git status was clean after inspection/execution. An initial sandbox python3 probe failed because python3 is not an executable inside that sandbox; the successful read-only scan and reproduction used node instead, without tooling changes. No service responses or integration evidence were fabricated. Product files remain untouched; only this review JSON was written. Release-only service/browser/deployment gates are listed separately and are not counted as code defects.
